function: Joint antenna selection, receive beamforming and device power scaling to minimize over-the-air aggregation error; solved by optimization (PDD, Lasso, FISTA), not trained (p. 8).
system: Uplink OTA-FL, single cell: K=50 single-antenna devices, server with N=128 antennas and L<N RF chains (16, 64, swept), fading Gaussian MAC; no RIS; band not stated (p. 6, 7, 21, 23).
method: Not learned: three optimization algorithms (penalty dual decomposition, box-Lasso, FISTA soft-thresholding) with alternating optimization; the learned element is a CNN trained by federated SGD (p. 4, 23).
data_channel: Custom simulator: path loss plus standard or correlated Rayleigh fading, devices uniform in a 10-100 m ring; FMNIST and CIFAR-10 for the FL task (p. 21-23).
test_conditions: CNN trained over 50 rounds and tested on held-out FMNIST/CIFAR-10 images; i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. splits, L=16 and 64, SNR sweep; channel changes every few rounds (p. 24-27).
baselines: Random antenna selection, greedy selection by channel gain [27], all-antenna selection, each with the paper's own alternating-optimization beamformer; no earlier published aggregation design or learned method (p. 22-23).
metrics: Aggregation error (dB) versus SNR and number of selected antennas L; test accuracy (%) versus communication rounds (p. 22-27).
complexity: Order derived: PDD Iout*Iin*K^3; Lasso and FISTA IAO*K^3, FISTA a constant factor faster; no runtime or operation counts (p. 19-20).
q1_support: p. 21: "For the fading process, we consider the Rayleigh model." - custom simulator (path loss plus Rayleigh, correlated Rayleigh after a textbook model); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 26: "the testing accuracy for the training of the CNN" - results are given per configuration (L, i.i.d. or non-i.i.d., Rayleigh or correlated); the paper never tests a model trained under one condition in another.
q3_support: p. 22: "we evaluate the performance for three baselines in addition to the proposed algorithms" - random, greedy and all-antenna policies, defined by the paper with its own beamformer; no earlier published aggregation design is compared.
q4_support: p. 19: "the overall complexity of Algorithm 1 scales with Iout Iin K 3" - order of complexity of the aggregation design; p. 19: "a computational complexity of order IAO K 3" for Lasso and FISTA.
q5_support: p. 23: "We consider 10-class image classification over CIFAR-10 [41] and FMNIST [42] datasets." - public datasets of the learning task only; channels are simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2305.17022v1) and prints no DOI; its title is 'Joint Antenna Selection and Beamforming for Massive MIMO-enabled Over-the-Air Federated Learning' and nothing indicates another paper. Included only through the OTA-FL rule of Step 1: the antenna selection and beamforming are classical optimization (p. 4-5), and the learned element is the CNN trained across the devices (p. 23). Area 7 because the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation (p. 8). The paper has no learned PHY baseline, hence q3=0; q4=1 for the derived complexity order of the aggregation design.
